deviations: next wiring: the packet phrases the turn-left traversal as 'the first outgoing half-edge of its destination vertex that is CCW of the twin'. The standard turn-left rule (which the packet also names) is the outgoing edge immediately CLOCKWISE of the twin -- the element immediately BEFORE the twin in the CCW-sorted angular order. With the literal CCW-of-twin reading, test 2's X traces ONE cycle around the crossing (a single face) instead of the four wedge walks the test asserts. The implementation uses the turn-left rule (element before twin) and documents the choice in the module doc.

Region winding is computed over the region's OWN boundary cycles, not over the whole profile. Over the full profile the M1 hole interior has winding 2 (the rectangle loop also winds around it), which contradicts the packet's asserted 'winding ±1' for both the plate and the hole; summing the winding of the region's representative point over the cycles in its `boundaries` gives plate = 1 and hole = 1 exactly as the packet asserts.

Test 2's four wedges: geometrically the complement of a FINITE X is connected (one region). The packet asserts four unbounded wedges, so the implementation models each maximal open face walk (a face boundary that terminates at degree-1 vertices) as its own unbounded region. Closed-loop profiles (tests 1, 5) are unaffected; a profile with both closed cycles and open walks folds the open walks into the exterior's boundary list.
disagreements: Stage 1 closed-loop rule vs test 2: the packet's Stage 1 says walk the profile in order and refuse with Contradictory when a curve's end does not equal the next curve's start, yet test 2 (two open segments that do not connect) must return Ok. The implementation builds chains by connectivity and refuses Contradictory only when a multi-curve chain fails to close; single open curves (test 2's two lines, test 3's single line) are accepted. A literal reading of Stage 1 would refuse test 2.

Winding value at the M1 hole: over the full profile (the packet's 'representative interior point over the profile loops'), the hole interior at (2,2) has winding 2 (rectangle 1 + circle 1), not the asserted ±1. Resolved by computing winding over the region's own boundary cycles (see deviations).
notes: Test 1 (rectangle with hole): exactly 3 regions observed (exterior winding 0, unbounded, boundaries == [[rectangle cycle]]; plate bounded, winding 1, boundaries [[rect cycle],[circle cycle]]; hole bounded, winding 1, boundaries [[circle cycle]]); vertex count 5 in the canonical no-split case (4 rectangle corners + the circle's single seam vertex; the full circle is one closed self-loop half-edge, no x-monotone split). next-wiring choice: PREDICATE (orient2d-based angular sort: half-plane split then orient2d cross-sign on the half-edge tangent at its origin), not atan2; the sort orders each vertex's incident half-edges CCW and next(e) is the element immediately before twin(e). Refusal path for the overlapping/coincident pair case: Refusal::Empty (the packet's decisive review choice), fired when two collinear segments overlap on a positive-length interval or two circles are coincident; parallel-but-not-collinear lines are not a refusal. A self-intersecting single loop (bowtie) is refused at the intersection stage with Refusal::Contradictory(DomainBoundary, False, True) on an interior same-chain contact, not at the region stage. Winding of test 2's four wedges is 0 by construction (open boundary walks enclose nothing). The Dyad substrate normalizes mantissas after every operation so intermediate products stay inside i128; the perfect-square discriminant check (sqrt_exact) is the honest refusal for algebraic vertices. The crate's errors::Result<T> alias (error type Error) shadows std's Result through the prelude, so the module uses an explicit S1Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, Refusal>. Certificate method is Method::Exact: vertex positions and crossing decisions are exact dyadic, and winding is decided by the exact orient2d predicate on the polygonized cycles, robust for the dyadic witnesses.
